summary: Rust/Buck2 local/static AC-0.11 evidence adds a who-gates-the-gates meta-check. It proves checked-in integrity-gate evidence carries known-bad fixtures, rejects vacuous pass conditions, requires self-mutation probes, and rejects oya CLI authority routing while keeping live required-context/P0.0/Phase-0/hyperscaler claims false.

red_evidence.expected_failure: assert-who-gates-gates.rs and //:who-gates-gates-check were absent before the slice.

green_evidence.rust_warning_policy: rustc --edition=2021 -D warnings for checker and Rust test harness
green_evidence.review_fix: Added BUCK as an explicit //:who-gates-gates-check src because the checker reads BUCK; tightened registry violation catalog to require oya_cli_authority_route.

rust_modern_standard_recorded.coverage_surface: Buck2-native LLVM source-based coverage remains the monorepo coverage direction; Tarpaulin is not canonical coverage evidence.
rust_modern_standard_recorded.mutation_surface: Dual Cargo.toml + Buck2/Reindeer remains the advisory local Cargo mutation-testing path while Buck2/cloud-ci evidence is authoritative for merge and Phase-0 claims.
rust_modern_standard_recorded.new_gate_surface: Rust checker + Rust self-test harness compile under Buck2 genrule with -D warnings; no new Python or shell gate/test surface for AC-0.11.
rust_modern_standard_recorded.hyperscaler_orientation: The gate is deterministic, target-addressable through Buck2, fixture-backed with explicit known-bad and self-mutation proofs, fail-closed on vacuous/authority-route regressions, and explicit about non-authority boundaries.
